acceptance_criteria.criterion: One repository-owned Railway runtime startup seam exists.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: railway.toml start command is updated to 'python scripts/railway_issuer_startup.py', the single canonical Railway start command pinned in the repository-owned configuration; no dashboard-only configuration can bypass it. scripts/railway_issuer_startup.py is the one startup seam bridging bootstrap and issuer launch, and it delegates entirely to the existing canonical bootstrap through the shared public contract (bootstrap_source_handling_authority.bootstrap_authority, the same function the bootstrap CLI calls) and to the canonical issuer (hunter_issue_agent_issuer.py).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Fresh mounted `/data` volume gets canonical root + genesis before issuer composition.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: test_fresh_volume_bootstrap_succeeds_and_issuer_launch_is_allowed proves the bootstrap completes before the issuer is exec'd, and verifies the operator root and genesis record exist in the database. test_fresh_volume_genesis_record_matches_production_rule verifies the genesis record ID matches the production rule.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Existing canonically bootstrapped volume is idempotent.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: test_existing_bootstrapped_volume_is_idempotent runs the startup seam twice and verifies the canonical_keys revision stays at 1 with unchanged record ID. test_existing_bootstrapped_volume_deterministic_across_restarts runs the startup seam three times and verifies exactly one authority record and one operator root.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Mismatched/tampered authority fails closed before issuer starts.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: test_tampered_signing_key_fails_closed proves a wrong signing key returns rc=1 with no issuer exec. test_mismatched_genesis_digest_fails_closed proves a tampered genesis digest fails closed. test_tampered_authority_preserved_after_mismatch_rejection proves the original authority is unchanged after rejection. test_bootstrap_failure_prevents_issuer_launch proves bootstrap failure prevents issuer launch.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Long-running issuer does not retain bootstrap signing authority.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: test_signing_key_scrubbed_from_issuer_environment verifies the signing key is absent from the issuer exec env. test_signing_key_still_present_during_bootstrap verifies the bootstrap receives the key. test_signing_key_never_appears_in_exec_env verifies the key value never appears in any env value passed to the issuer.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `/healthz` becomes healthy on Railway after canonical bootstrap.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: This review establishes the implementation precondition: the startup seam composes the issuer only after the canonical bootstrap of the mounted volume, so the issuer's /healthz handler can only become reachable after the authority database exists on the mounted /data volume. test_issuer_launch_cannot_happen_before_successful_bootstrap and test_bootstrap_failure_prevents_issuer_launch prove the issuer process only starts after canonical bootstrap, and test_evidence_directory_without_a_mounted_volume_fails_closed proves the seam fails closed before bootstrap when the volume is not mounted. Live operational proof -- /healthz returning healthy on a deployed Railway service -- is still to be verified after deployment is authorized and is not claimed by this review.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Focused tests cover fresh, idempotent, mismatch, and signing-key-lifecycle cases.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: 21 tests in test_railway_issuer_startup.py cover fresh-volume bootstrap (2), mounted-volume verification (3), already-bootstrapped idempotency (2), tamper/mismatch fail-closed (3), configuration fail-closed (2), signing-key lifecycle isolation (3), bootstrap-before-issuer ordering (2), canonical issuer command, provenance resolver and port (3), and the shared public bootstrap contract (1). All 21 pass, alongside the pre-existing bootstrap/issuer suites.

railway.toml start command 'python scripts/railway_issuer_startup.py' matches the Railway section of docs/ISSUE_AGENT_ISSUER_DEPLOYMENT.md, which documents runtime bootstrap of the mounted /data volume as the canonical startup path and sequences per-Issue provisioning strictly after the deploying bootstrap (the genesis rule must already exist in the database), plus the signature lifecycle contract. No dashboard-only Railway configuration is introduced.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Normal pre-push, hostile review, exact-head hosted gates green.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The normal pre-push hook passes on this exact head and reports READY-ELIGIBLE only after the exact-head hostile review covers every governing Issue criterion. This artifact is the hostile review bound to this head, and exact-head hosted gates are the authoritative remaining proof target.

acceptance_criteria.evidence: PR #443 is opened as Draft. No Ready promotion, no merge, and no Railway deployment are performed; owner approval is required before any of those states change.

defect_families.evidence: No caller-controlled temporal authority is introduced; the bootstrap uses the current UTC instant and the issuer uses its own clock, both unchanged.
No persistence or transaction boundary is altered; the startup seam delegates to the existing bootstrap which uses the same SQLite transaction semantics.
No logical identity is reused; the startup seam adds no new identity authority.
No schema vocabulary is added or weakened; the bootstrap outcome is machine-readable JSON and the issuer configuration schema is unchanged.
No persistence-permission vocabulary changes; the bootstrap writes to the same tables the existing canonical path uses.
The startup seam is deterministic: same inputs produce same bootstrap outcome, same issuer exec argv, and same environment scrubbing.
No authorization vocabulary or binding changes; the startup seam does not alter the issuer's authorization verification path.

No tamper or history forgery surface is introduced; the startup seam delegates to the existing canonical bootstrap which uses the same append-only authority persistence. The signing key is consumed from the environment and never printed or committed.
No connector provenance evidence lifecycle is altered; the startup seam operates before the issuer and does not touch provenance records.
All candidate commits are signed by the authorized identity on the governed clone path; writer provenance covers the range.
The review excludes its own artifact path and its review_id is the SHA-256 of exactly its claims, so hand-editing is detectable.
The inherited connector authorization receipt makes no new candidate claim; only this canonical hostile-review artifact is refreshed for the exact #442 candidate head.

No Ready or READY-ELIGIBLE signal exists without a complete exact-head hostile review: the local pre-push boundary derives the governing Issue acceptance criteria from GitHub and fails closed (DRAFT-ONLY) unless every Issue #442 criterion is covered, so a review cannot inflate readiness on its own.
No hosted prerequisite/controller logic changes; running exact-head hosted CI remains pending.
The defect-registry addition DFF-019 is narrow and regression-tested; the preflight guard validates it.
No validation proof reuse surface is changed; the startup seam does not interact with validation receipts or the pre-push hook.
No engineering-task ingress or compiled-budget path is altered; the startup seam operates before issuer composition.

The new DFF-019 family declares runtime-bootstrap-not-volume-aware-before-issuer-composition prevention with 21 regression tests covering fresh volume, mounted-volume verification, idempotency, tamper/mismatch fail-closed, signing-key lifecycle isolation, ordering invariants, and the shared public bootstrap contract.

findings.evidence: The original deployment path ran the issuer directly via railway.toml start command without any bootstrap. Railway volumes are not mounted during preDeploy, so a one-off bootstrap job could not access /data. The startup seam (railway_issuer_startup.py) bridges this gap by idempotently bootstrapping at runtime after the volume is mounted but before the issuer starts.

The signing key (HUNTER_SOURCE_HANDLING_SIGNING_KEY) was previously required to be manually removed from the Railway Service after bootstrap. The startup seam now consumes the key for bootstrap and scrubs it from the process environment before exec'ing the issuer, so the signing key can remain as a Railway Secret without reaching the issuer process.

No parallel bootstrap, no parallel issuer, no duplicate authority model. The startup seam delegates entirely to the existing canonical bootstrap_source_handling_authority and exec's the existing canonical hunter_issue_agent_issuer.py with the same provenance resolver.

DFF-019 is added to docs/DEFECT_REGISTRY.json with scope scripts/ and railway.toml, and 18 regression test references. The preflight guard recomputes applicable families from changed paths, so any future deployment path that bypasses the startup seam is review-blocked.
